- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 3–5 days at 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) or shows strong reversal, model overreacts; reduce forecast mean by 1–2% and shift downward trend.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or weak (0.0–0.3), especially if recent price is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 5-day average is >10% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” spikes, model tends to overreact; apply a 0.5–1.0% dampening factor to forecast peaks.
- When sentiment is mixed or trending sideways, model often overfits short-term noise; use 30-day moving average as baseline for correction.
